payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: The guide you sent is version 3.2 from 2014 and describes extract format 3.x, but the manifest says 4.0. Which is current, and what changed?
4.0 is current, since the 2019 upgrade. The guide never got updated. 4.0 added the LOINC column in TESTDICT and the TH visit type. Treat the guide as a 3.x document.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: The guide lists IMMUNE.DAT, but there is no such file in the export. Is it missing from this delivery?
No. There is no IMMUNE.DAT. It was in the vendor's guide but we never kept immunizations in MCS/2; the state registry is the record.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: Can you confirm the file format: delimiter, header row, encoding, quoting?
Pipe-delimited, header row on every file, Latin-1, CRLF line ends, no quoting. Pipes are not allowed in data.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: The guide says every timestamp is Mountain Time. Is that true for both campuses, including Sun Ridge in Tucson?

No. HVMC is Mountain local time with daylight saving. Sun Ridge is in Tucson: Arizona does not do daylight saving, and Sun Ridge timestamps are Arizona local time all year. Treat SRC as America/Phoenix and HVMC as America/Denver.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: How do I tell which campus a timestamp belongs to?
Visits and appointments through the clinic's campus, CLINIC.CAMPUS_CD. Everything else through the patient's registration campus, PERSON.CAMPUS_CD.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: VISIT_TYPE has TH in 223 rows, which the guide does not list, and 11 rows keyed in lowercase (th, op, er, sds). What are they?
TH is telehealth, video visits, since 2020. SDS is same-day surgery, outpatient procedural. Lowercase is just how someone typed it; the field isn't validated. th is TH.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: VS_UNIT is blank on 92% of vital-sign rows. What unit are the blank ones in?

HVMC's flowsheet never sends a unit. Everything there is US units: weight pounds, temperature Fahrenheit, height inches. Sun Ridge's flowsheet sends metric with the unit filled in: kg, C, cm. HR, RR and SPO2 never carry a unit at either campus. BP is systolic/diastolic.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: There are 132 Sun Ridge weight, temperature and height rows with a blank unit, all taken before March 2016, and the blank temperatures read 97 to 100. Where did those come from?
payload.why: VITALS.VS_UNIT follow-up (132 SRC blank-unit rows, all before 2016-03)

payload.text: That's the migration. When we moved Sun Ridge onto MCS/2 in March 2016 we loaded their history from the old system as-is, flowsheets included. I didn't map their flowsheet myself. I think their old system was set up in American units, but I wouldn't swear to it. Temperatures of 97 to 100 would be Fahrenheit, though.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: What does VISIT STATUS VOID mean?
Entered in error. That's what the guide says and what the status means.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: How are patients keyed across files, and can one person have more than one PERSON_NO?

PERSON_NO joins everything; MRN is enterprise-wide. But yes: the 2016 MPI project only matched patients inside each campus. Patients seen at both HVMC and Sun Ridge before 2016 still have two registrations, one per campus, and nobody linked them. Same-campus duplicate registrations still happen too.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: APPT_STATUS has BMP in 19 rows. What does it mean?
Scheduling is a vendor-hosted module; I pass through what it writes. I don't know what BMP means. Ask the vendor or the clinics.

payload.name: Gary-Lindqvist
payload.text: Lab collection timestamps come in two formats: 01-APR-14 09:14 on most rows, and 2024-03-05 08:15 on 115 Sun Ridge rows from 2024 on. Why?
The lab interface writes what the lab system sends; I don't reformat. Ask Ray.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: SEX_CD is 1, 2, 9 or 3. The guide has 1, 2 and 9. What is 3?
1 male, 2 female, 9 unknown. Since 2021 we record 3 for patients whose documents carry an X marker. Zero is not something anyone keys.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: Six patients have a birth date of 01/01/1900. Are those real?
No. When a patient can't give a date of birth the desk keys 01/01/1900 so the registration can be saved. It is a placeholder, not a birth date; HIM is supposed to chase it, and some never got fixed.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: Coverage relationship codes are S, P, C, O, and on 11 rows D. The guide says S, SP, D, O. What do your desks key, and what is D?

S self, P spouse or partner, C child, O other. Some coverages were saved with it blank. D isn't one of ours. If it's on old Sun Ridge coverages, that's how Sun Ridge did things before they joined us in 2016. Their old registrations came over in the migration; I didn't build that.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: What values can RACE_TXT hold?

The picklist text: White, Black or African American, Asian, Hispanic or Latino, American Indian/Alaska Native, Pacific Islander, Other, Declined. Yes, Hispanic is on the race picklist; it should have been an ethnicity question.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: What does NKA_YN mean, and can it disagree with the allergy file?
Y means the patient told the desk no known allergies. Nurses sometimes add allergies later without clearing it, so yes.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: Problem codes come both with a decimal point (250.00) and without (E119). Which is right?

Both, depending on age. MCS/2 strips the decimal point when it stores a code, ever since the 2012 upgrade. Anything entered before that kept its point. E11.9 is stored E119 now, 250.00 is stored 25000.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: When is a problem coded ICD-9 versus ICD-10, and what are problems with no code?
ICD-10 since October 2015, ICD-9 before that. Problems entered without a code are free text the provider typed.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: Can one patient have more than one PERSON_NO?
The 2016 MPI project merged every duplicate registration at both campuses. Since then there is one PERSON_NO per person. If you find two, it's a desk error from last week, not history.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: Do both campuses chart in the same time zone?
We are one health system on one clock: everything in MCS/2 is Mountain Time.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: What does a VOID visit mean? I see 25 of them; 11 are ER visits from 2018 on that have vital signs recorded.

HIM voids a visit that was registered in error. And since 2018 the ED registrars also VOID the visit when a patient leaves without being seen, because MCS/2 has no other way to close it. Those patients were really there: triage took their vitals. They are not errors and shouldn't vanish from the chart.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: How do I tell a left-without-being-seen VOID from an error VOID?
It's an ED visit and triage has vitals on it. An error VOID never got that far.

payload.name: Denise-Okafor
payload.text: Appointment status BMP: do you know what it means?
That's not mine. Scheduling sits with the clinics and IT. Ask Gary.

payload.name: Ray-Castillo
payload.text: COLLECTED_TS comes in two formats: 14-MAR-23 08:15 on most rows and 2024-03-05 08:15 on 115 Sun Ridge rows from 2024 on. How should each be read, and in which time zone?

The lab interface writes Oracle-style: day, three-letter month, two-digit year, then 24-hour time, like 14-MAR-23 08:15. Every lab row is from 2005 or later, so the two-digit year is always 20xx. It's local time at the collecting campus. I don't know about any other format.

payload.name: Ray-Castillo
payload.text: RESULT_STATUS has F, C and X. What do they mean?
F final, C corrected; the value on the row is the corrected value. Cancelled results are purged before the nightly extract, so you won't see them.

payload.name: Ray-Castillo
payload.text: There are 54 rows with RESULT_STATUS X, 22 of them with the result text CANCELLED. If cancelled results are purged, what are these?

That's the only status I know of besides F and C. If you see X with CANCELLED in the result, those are cancelled orders. They shouldn't be in there, and they certainly should not go into the new chart.

payload.name: Ray-Castillo
payload.text: Where do LOINC codes for your tests come from, and which tests have none?

I loaded the LOINC column in TESTDICT in 2019 for every orderable test. SENDOUT is the miscellaneous send-out bucket: the real test is whatever the reference lab ran and the result is a scanned report, so it has no LOINC and never will.

payload.name: Ray-Castillo
payload.text: What is in RESULT and UNITS? I see mmol/L on some glucose rows.

RESULT is the result as released: numbers, NEG/POS for qualitative tests, or text like SEE SCANNED REPORT for send-outs. UNITS is what the instrument reported. Sun Ridge's analyzer reports glucose in mmol/L, HVMC mg/dL. Both are right.

payload.name: Ray-Castillo
payload.text: What are the ABN flag values?
H high, L low, A abnormal for positives.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: DRUGFILE.RXNORM is blank on three drugs. What are they, and are they still used?
Rows without RxNorm are the compounded items and the MISC placeholder, and they only sit on old orders that are long inactive. Nothing current uses them; you can skip them safely.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: MD0105 has no RxNorm in the drug file and appears on 33 orders. What is it?
MD0105 is insulin glargine 100 units/mL. Its RxNorm is 285018. I'm sure of that one; I just never got it into the drug file.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: And MD0190 and MD0199?
MD0190 is a compounded mouthwash and has no single RxNorm concept. MD0199 is MISC MEDICATION - SEE COMMENT: the actual drug is in a free-text comment we don't extract.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: The drug file gives MD0108, levothyroxine 50 mcg, RxNorm 966221. Our RxNorm reference has levothyroxine 50 mcg oral tablet as 966222. Which is right?
I backfilled every drug file row by hand in 2018 and double-checked them. They are right.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: What does RX_STATUS HOLD mean for the conversion?
In practice HOLD is how prescribers park a medication they've stopped. Treat HOLD as discontinued.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: What do SIG_TXT and DOSE_TXT hold?
SIG_TXT is the sig as the prescriber typed it, mostly Latin abbreviations. DOSE_TXT is the dose with its unit.

payload.name: Priya-Natarajan
payload.text: Who maintains allergy entries?
Registration and nursing own allergies. Ask Denise.
